org.Hs.eg.ice 0.1.1
  • Reference
    • Querying human gene annotation via biocOnIce with org.Hs.eg.ice

org.Hs.eg.ice

A demonstration package: human gene annotation from the biocOnIce public Iceberg catalog, queried directly with dplyr/DBI, with no dependency on AnnotationDbi — no OrgDb class, no Bimap objects, no select()/mapIds()/keytypes() keytype whitelist. See PlanFor3.24.md Milestone 7 in the BioconductorAnnotationPipeline repository for why.

Four accessors, each a lazy dplyr table already filtered to human (taxon_id = 9606) and to currently-valid rows:

  • hs_gene() — annotation.ncbi__gene: gene_id, symbol, description, gene_type, chromosome, map_location.
  • hs_alias() — annotation.identifier_mapping: every cross-reference namespace NCBI/Ensembl assert, discriminated by source_namespace/ target_namespace.
  • hs_go() — annotation.ncbi__gene_go: direct GO annotations, go_id/ evidence/qualifier/category.
  • hs_pubmed() — annotation.ncbi__gene_pubmed: gene_id/pubmed_id.

Each one adds nothing beyond that filter — every join, every column selection, is ordinary dplyr written by the caller against the lazy table.

The comparison this package exists to make

The AnnotationDbi way:

library(org.Hs.eg.db)
mapIds(org.Hs.eg.db, keys = "TP53", keytype = "SYMBOL", column = "ENTREZID")
select(org.Hs.eg.db, keys = "TP53", keytype = "SYMBOL",
       columns = c("ENTREZID", "GENENAME"))

The direct way:

library(org.Hs.eg.ice)
library(dplyr)

hs_gene() |>
    filter(symbol == "TP53") |>
    select(gene_id, symbol, description) |>
    collect()

A join select()/mapIds() cannot express in one call — symbol to its direct GO annotations:

hs_gene() |>
    filter(symbol == "TP53") |>
    inner_join(hs_go(), by = c("gene_id", "taxon_id")) |>
    select(symbol, go_id, go_term, evidence, category) |>
    collect()

OrgDb’s GOALL (the ancestor closure over the GO DAG) needs ontology.relationship, a table this package does not wrap — attach it directly, as bioc-on-ice’s own README shows for cell types:

con <- ice_con()
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "
    WITH RECURSIVE ancestors(go_id) AS (
        SELECT go_id FROM bioc.annotation.ncbi__gene_go
        WHERE gene_id = '7157' AND taxon_id = 9606 AND valid_to IS NULL
        UNION
        SELECT r.object_id
        FROM bioc.ontology.relationship r
        JOIN ancestors a ON r.subject_id = a.go_id
        WHERE r.predicate = 'is_a' AND r.ontology = 'go' AND r.valid_to IS NULL
    )
    SELECT DISTINCT t.term_id, t.name
    FROM ancestors a
    JOIN bioc.ontology.term t ON t.term_id = a.go_id AND t.valid_to IS NULL;
")

That query is exactly what GOALL/select(..., columns = "GOALL") can never return in one AnnotationDbi call — this package doesn’t need to invent an API for it, because the recursive CTE is already SQL.

AnnotationDbi concept → org.Hs.eg.ice equivalent

AnnotationDbi concept (org.Hs.eg.db) org.Hs.eg.db org.Hs.eg.ice
Object model OrgDb S4 class, Bimap objects under the hood No class at all — four plain dplyr::tbl() lazy tables (hs_gene(), hs_alias(), hs_go(), hs_pubmed())
keytypes(x) Returns fixed whitelist (ENTREZID, SYMBOL, ALIAS, ENSEMBL, GO, PMID, …) No such function/concept. “Keytype” is just whichever column you filter() on — e.g. hs_alias() \|> filter(target_namespace == "ALIAS") is OrgDb’s ALIAS keytype, filter(target_namespace == "ENSEMBL") is ENSEMBL, etc.
columns(x) Fixed list of retrievable columns No enumeration function — the columns are whatever’s in the four tables’ schemas (visible via colnames()/glimpse() on the lazy table itself)
select(x, keys, keytype, columns) One call does filter + column choice + join across internal tables No equivalent call; it’s ordinary dplyr::filter() + select() + left_join()/inner_join() written by the caller against the lazy tables
mapIds(x, keys, keytype, column) Single-valued key→value lookup, with multiVals disambiguation logic No equivalent; same filter()+select()+collect() pattern, caller handles 1:many themselves (e.g. nrow()>1 just means multiple rows come back)
ENTREZID Row names / keytype hs_gene()$gene_id
SYMBOL keytype/column hs_gene()$symbol
GENENAME column hs_gene()$description
GENETYPE column hs_gene()$gene_type
CHR column hs_gene()$chromosome
MAP column hs_gene()$map_location
ALIAS, ENSEMBL, HGNC, MIM, … separate keytypes, each its own internal mapping table all rows of hs_alias() (annotation.identifier_mapping), discriminated by source_namespace/target_namespace rather than being separate keytypes
GO (direct annotations) column, via select(..., columns="GO") hs_go(): go_id, evidence, qualifier, category
GOALL (ancestor closure over the GO DAG) precomputed column, one select() call not precomputed — a hand-written WITH RECURSIVE CTE over ontology.relationship/ontology.term (above); the DAG walk is explicit SQL, not a library feature
PMID column hs_pubmed()$pubmed_id
Multi-table joins (e.g. symbol → GO → PubMed in one call) not expressible in a single select()/mapIds() call — requires multiple calls and manual merging ordinary dplyr joins across the four lazy tables in one pipeline, same as joining any other tables
Offline / cold-start speed instant, local SQLite, ~0.1s/query live: ~4–16s/query (S3/catalog metadata overhead per call, independent of result size)
Local caching implicit — the whole package is a local cache (a shipped SQLite file) opt-in: ice_cache_refresh() materializes all four tables into a local BiocFileCache-managed DuckDB file; cache = TRUE on any accessor reads from it (~0.09s/query once refreshed, see Milestone 8 below)
Versioning / reproducibility pinned to the installed package version not yet addressed by the cache; live data reflects bioc-on-ice’s row-level valid_from/valid_to/provenance.release model — open question (PlanFor3.24.md Milestone 8) whether joins across tables are point-in-time consistent
Dependencies AnnotationDbi, RSQLite, Bioconductor infrastructure DBI, dbplyr, dplyr, duckdb, BiocFileCache (cache only) — no AnnotationDbi dependency at all

The throughline: org.Hs.eg.db hides its schema behind a fixed keytype/column API that select()/mapIds() interpret; org.Hs.eg.ice exposes the schema directly as lazy tables and leaves the “keytype” logic (which column, which namespace) to ordinary dplyr verbs the caller writes.

Connecting 

library(org.Hs.eg.ice)
hs_gene()   # opens the shared connection (ice_con()) on first use, anonymous, no token

Every accessor takes an explicit con argument if you want an independent connection instead of the package’s shared one:

con <- connect_ice()
hs_gene(con)
disconnect_ice(con)

Local caching (provisional, Milestone 8)

Every accessor above stays live by default. If the live-catalog latency is a problem for a session, ice_cache_refresh() pulls all four tables once into a local BiocFileCache-managed DuckDB file; pass cache = TRUE to any accessor to read from it instead of the live catalog:

library(org.Hs.eg.ice)
ice_cache_refresh()                       # one-time, explicit, slow call

hs_gene(cache = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::filter(symbol == "ORMDL3") |>
    dplyr::left_join(hs_pubmed(cache = TRUE), by = "gene_id") |>
    dplyr::collect()

Nothing calls ice_cache_refresh() automatically, and nothing expires the cache automatically – call it again when you want a fresher copy, or ice_cache_clear() to remove it. This is a provisional implementation of PlanFor3.24.md Milestone 8, built to demonstrate the latency difference; it does not yet tag the cache with a bioc-on-ice provenance.release identifier, and makes no cross-table-consistency claim beyond what the live catalog itself provides (see Milestone 8’s open caveat on that).

A real end-to-end run (2026-10-22) confirmed the speedup: hs_gene(cache=TRUE) |> filter(symbol=="ORMDL3") |> collect() took 0.090s versus 15.987s live. The refresh itself took ~869s total, almost entirely alias/identifier_mapping (6.59M rows, ~739s) – gene, go, and pubmed together took well under two minutes. ice_cache_refresh() prints per-table progress (pulling ... / N rows in Ns) since this isn’t fast enough to run silently. If you don’t need hs_alias() (cross-reference lookups), ice_cache_refresh(skip_alias = TRUE) skips it and cuts the refresh to well under two minutes; hs_alias(cache = TRUE) then errors telling you to refresh again without skip_alias.

Status

Four accessors (PlanFor3.24.md Milestone 7) plus a provisional local cache (Milestone 8, above). Real tests exist: tests/testthat/ test-accessors.R has live-catalog tests (skips cleanly if the catalog is unreachable) and offline signature/cache-state checks. A Quarto vignette (vignettes/org.Hs.eg.ice.qmd) documents the workflow but isn’t evaluated at build time yet (execute: eval: false), since the package hasn’t been R CMD checked against the live catalog in a build/CI environment. Not published.
